subject: ENGLISH 10
pageTitle: Active vs Passive Voice: How to Tell and When to Use Each
description: Identify active and passive voice, rewrite passive sentences, and decide when passive is the better choice, with two worked examples.
caption: Active vs passive voice in 7 swipes: how to spot each, how to fix it, and when passive is fine. Save this for your writing unit. Free English 10 study guide at precisstudy.com/english-10 (no sign-up).

slides.title: HOW TO TELL
lines: Active: the subject does the action
Passive: the subject receives the action
Passive often uses was/were/is + past participle
slides.note: Test: add 'by zombies' after the verb. If it works, it is passive.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: Rewrite in active voice: 'The ball was thrown by Mia.'
steps: Find who does the action: Mia

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: Rewrite in active voice: 'Mistakes were made.'
steps: Name the doer to be clear

slides.title: WATCH OUT
points: Use passive when the doer is unknown or unimportant.
Use passive in science writing: 'The solution was heated.'
Use active most of the time for clear, direct writing.
